original_question: Show that the hypersurface X = {x + x^2 y + z^3 + t^2 = 0} in C^4, which is known to be an exotic C^3, is not biholomorphic to C^3; more generally, show the same for other known hypersurfaces in C^n that are exotic C^(n-1) varieties.
target_in_paper: Section 1, centered on Conjecture 1.1: whether an exotic algebraic structure on C^n can be analytically trivial, i.e. biholomorphic to the standard C^n; with Proposition 1.2 giving the proved hyperbolic/log-general-type case and Theorem 1.3 supplying many analytically distinct exotic examples. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9506006))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's core theme: the mismatch between algebraic and holomorphic equivalence for exotic affine spaces, and it focuses on the question 'not biholomorphic to C^n' rather than merely 'not algebraically isomorphic to C^n'. It also points to a contractible/exotic threefold hypersurface as a motivating example, which is in the right neighborhood of the paper's discussion. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1993__217__251_0.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's formulation is an open conjectural/research question, not a theorem to be proved; your draft incorrectly says 'Show that'.
The official target is not restricted to one hypersurface or even to hypersurfaces; it asks the general analytic-triviality question for exotic algebraic structures on C^n.
You need to define 'exotic C^n' paper-faithfully: a smooth affine complex algebraic variety that is diffeomorphic to R^{2n} but not algebraically isomorphic to C^n.
The ambient field/category must be stated: complex affine algebraic varieties over C, and biholomorphism in the complex-analytic sense.
The nearby paper context separates a proved partial case from the conjecture: hyperbolic/log-general-type examples are known not to be biholomorphic to C^n, but the general problem remains open.
Your draft broadens to 'other known hypersurfaces in C^n that are exotic C^(n-1) varieties', which is not the paper's nearest official formulation.
If one wants to retain the specific Russell/Koras-Russell cubic, it should appear only as an instance or 'in particular' clause, not as the main paper-faithful statement.
The nearby existence theorem concerns dimensions n >= 3 and gives countably many pairwise biholomorphically nonequivalent exotic structures; that contextual quantifier is missing.
refined_question: Let X be a smooth affine algebraic variety over C which is diffeomorphic to R^{2n} but not algebraically isomorphic to C^n (that is, an exotic algebraic structure on C^n). Must X fail to be biholomorphic to C^n as a complex analytic manifold?
justification: The draft is trying to capture the paper's analytic version of the exotic-affine-space problem, but it overshoots in two ways: it turns the problem into a proof request, and it narrows the official formulation to one hypersurface plus an extra hypersurface-generalization that the paper itself does not use as its main statement. The surrounding results show the intended structure: a general conjecture about all exotic C^n's, a proved special case for hyperbolic/log-general-type examples, and an existence theorem producing many pairwise biholomorphically nonequivalent exotic affine spaces in dimensions at least 3. That is why the refined question above is the closest stand-alone reformulation of the paper's actual intent. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1993__217__251_0.pdf))
